sources.cite: Terraform tutorial, Run a refresh-only operation (HashiCorp Developer)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: drift is resources no longer matching state; a refresh-only run updates state without changing resources; you then either accept the new value and update the configuration, or reapply the configuration to revert the resource.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: where the backend supports it, Terraform locks state for every operation that could write it; force-unlock is only for your own lock after automatic unlocking failed, since unlocking someone else's risks concurrent writes.
The organization, the systems and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You run infrastructure automation at Kestrel Bank, a fictional bank. Terraform manages the network and servers. This morning's plan shows unexpected changes.
handover: A plan shows the payments security group changing back: someone opened SSH to 0.0.0.0/0 in the console.
The network and server teams each keep their own copy of state.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: scanners find SSH open on the payments servers; brute-force attempts begin within the hour.
Check-in 3: both applies write state; terraform loses track of three subnets and plans to recreate them.
Check-in 4: an engineer applies from a stale copy; terraform creates duplicate servers and the bill doubles.

driftPrompt.title: Accept or revert the drift?
driftPrompt.context: Someone opened SSH to the world in the console.

choices.label: Apply the configuration to remove the console rule, find out who opened it and why, and schedule a daily refresh-only plan that alerts on drift

effects.log: The rule is gone; drift is checked daily.

choices.feedback: Drift is real resources no longer matching state; reapplying configuration reverts an unwanted change, and regular checks catch the next one.

choices.label: Delete the rule in the console

effects.log: The rule is removed by hand.

choices.feedback: Fixed today, but nothing will notice the next drift.

choices.label: Accept it: apply refresh-only and add the rule to the configuration

effects.log: The open rule is now in state and code.

choices.feedback: Accepting drift writes SSH-to-the-world into the bank's configuration.

lockPrompt.title: Error acquiring the state lock
lockPrompt.context: A colleague's apply fails; a pipeline run holds the lock.

choices.label: Check who holds the lock, wait for the pipeline run to finish, then apply; use force-unlock only for your own stuck lock

effects.log: The pipeline finishes; the apply runs cleanly.

choices.feedback: Locking prevents concurrent writes to state; force-unlock is only for your own lock when automatic unlocking failed.

choices.label: Cancel the pipeline run to free the lock
choices.feedback: The lock frees, but a half-finished apply may leave resources out of step.

choices.label: terraform force-unlock the pipeline's lock and apply now
choices.feedback: Two applies now write state at once.

statePrompt.title: State on a laptop
statePrompt.context: The server team's state lives on one laptop.

choices.label: Migrate the server team's state to the remote backend with locking and restricted access, and remove local copies

effects.log: Both teams use locked remote state.

choices.feedback: A shared backend with locking gives one authoritative state and prevents concurrent writes.

choices.label: Put the state file on a shared drive

effects.log: State is on a shared drive.

choices.feedback: Everyone sees it, but two engineers can still write at once.

choices.label: Keep local state; it has worked so far
choices.feedback: One lost or stale laptop means terraform no longer knows what it manages.

scoring.modelReasoning: Configuration management keeps real resources matching declared configuration. Detect drift with refresh-only plans; revert unwanted drift by reapplying configuration, and accept drift only when it is intended. State needs one authoritative, locked home: never force another run's lock, and never keep state on a laptop.
